Master’s thesis · Web application

Making Thinking Visible: AI Mathematics Companion

Independently built a mathematics learning system combining an interactive canvas and cooperating AI agents. Students express their reasoning through handwriting, drawings, and text, receiving guidance adapted to their problem-solving stage.

  • Web
  • Multimodal AI
  • Interactive canvas
  • Multi-agent

My contribution

Independently developed the complete system, including the interactive canvas, backend and data records, AI-agent coordination, prompt strategies, and feature integration. Questionnaires and scales used for research analysis drew on published literature and instruments used by senior researchers.

Period：2026

Making the reasoning process visible

The interface brings together geometric word problems, an interactive canvas, and AI conversation for upper-elementary students. Handwriting, geometric drawing, equations, image uploads, and annotations preserve students’ evolving reasoning and revisions.

Three layers and agent responsibilities

The interaction layer provides a responsive interface, canvas, and conversation. In the intelligence layer, a mathematical-thinking analyst estimates the problem-solving stage, while an AI helper combines core and stage-specific prompts to generate guidance. The data layer stores tasks, dialogue, canvas events, and learning records.

Data flow for one interaction

When a student sends a message, the system collects the canvas image and recent interaction history. The analyst estimates the current stage, and the helper uses that result and task context to generate questions or empathetic responses. Dialogue and activity records are then updated for the next interaction. The design supports reasoning rather than simply revealing answers.

Pilot observations and limitations

The pilot included nine fifth graders and observed interactions combining text and canvas activity. Pre–post differences in mathematics anxiety and self-efficacy were not statistically significant, so the study does not establish improved learning outcomes. Further work includes validating stage estimates, understanding irregular handwriting, and reducing repetitive responses.
